correctness.rationale: Uniform circular spacings have Dirichlet(1,...,1) joint law; identical, adjacent, and nonadjacent vertex-pair events yield exact two-, three-, and four-gap simplex probabilities. The normalized covariance is strictly decreasing up to its plateau, and its terminal sign is the sign of 1-n(1-2t)^(n-1); positive variance at equal radii fixes the complete classification. Uniform first-order expansion yields the sparse crossover. The standalone exact rational checker passed 1673 enumerations/sign/asymptotic assertions; finite checks corroborate but are not substitutes for the mathematical proof.

value.rationale: The number of isolated vertices is a natural graph-connectivity observable; nested radii yield a nonobvious exact negative covariance region despite pathwise monotonicity. The theorem classifies all finite radii, identifies the expected-one critical boundary and an extended zero-covariance plateau, and provides an explicit sparse correlation frontier. These structural results inform joint multiscale isolation diagnostics; no test-power improvement or universal association is asserted.
